definitions.rationale: This equation expands the named anyIntBody proof term into the translated function body, so it is a macro-like definition rather than an additional mathematical fact.
definitions.text:
rule anyIntBody
    => Return(
         BoolOp(
           "and",
           Call(Name("isinstance"), Name("x"), Name("int")),
           Call(Name("isinstance"), Name("y"), Name("int")),
           Call(Name("isinstance"), Name("z"), Name("int")),
           BoolOp(
             "or",
             Compare(
               BinOp("+", Name("x"), Name("y")),
               CmpOp("==", Name("z"))),
             Compare(
               BinOp("+", Name("x"), Name("z")),
               CmpOp("==", Name("y"))),
             Compare(
               BinOp("+", Name("y"), Name("z")),
               CmpOp("==", Name("x"))))))
       .Stmts

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the named sumCondition summary as the disjunction of the three integer sum equalities used in the specification.
definitions.text:
rule sumCondition(X:Int, Y:Int, Z:Int)
    => ((X +Int Y) ==Int Z)
       orBool ((X +Int Z) ==Int Y)
       orBool ((Y +Int Z) ==Int X)

operational_rules.rationale: This k-cell transition invokes the modeled function by constructing its closure and applying it to the three argument values, making it an ordinary execution rule in the verification model.
operational_rules.text:
rule <k> #anyInt(X:Val, Y:Val, Z:Val)
        => #applyK(
             toCall(closureVal(("x", "y", "z"), anyIntBody, 0)),
             (X, Y, Z, .Vals))
         ... </k>
